title: CCTV and enforcement rules for pet grooming businesses
asked: Ms Jessica Tan asked whether AVS will consider mandatory CCTV recordings in pet grooming facilities and require licensed operators to retain footage for investigations. She also asked what measures are being taken to strengthen enforcement against pet businesses that breach the Animals and Birds Act and Code of Animal Welfare, and whether serious negligence causing animal harm or death may lead to enhanced penalties or longer licence suspensions.
response: Mr Alvin Tan said individuals in animal-related businesses face higher maximum penalties under the Animals and Birds Act for animal cruelty and welfare offences, and failure to meet Code of Animal Welfare standards may be used as evidence for enforcement action. A court may issue a disqualification order of up to 12 months, and NParks has investigated 54 cases of feedback alleging harm to pets by groomers over the past three years. The regulatory regime for pet sector activities, including pet grooming, is under review, and the ministry will consider CCTV requirements when amending legislation and is reviewing penalties for animal welfare and cruelty offences. He added that the Code specifies minimum standards and best practices, including not leaving animals unattended, and breaches can support prosecution under sections 42 and 41 of the Act.

key_points.point: Individuals in animal-related businesses face higher maximum penalties under the Animals and Birds Act for animal cruelty and welfare offences than the general public.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: these individuals face higher maximum penalties under the Animals and Birds Act (ABA) for animal cruelty and welfare offences compared to other members of the public

key_points.point: Failure to meet minimum standards under the Code of Animal Welfare may be used as evidence for enforcement action.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: Failure to meet minimum standards stipulated under the Code of Animal Welfare may be used as evidence for enforcement action.

key_points.point: A court may issue a disqualification order of up to 12 months from owning an animal or running an animal-related business.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: the Court may also issue a disqualification order to an individual to disqualify them from owning an animal or running an animal-related business for up to 12 months

key_points.point: NParks has investigated 54 cases of feedback alleging harm to pets caused by groomers over the past three years.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: The National Parks Board (NParks) has investigated 54 cases of feedback alleging harm to pets caused by groomers over the past three years.

key_points.point: The regulatory regime for pet sector activities, including pet grooming businesses, is under review as part of the ABA review.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: We are reviewing the regulatory regime for pet sector activities, including pet grooming businesses, under the ongoing review of the ABA.

key_points.point: The ministry will consider whether to include CCTV recording requirements when amending the legislation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: We will consider whether to include requirements for closed circuit television (CCTV) recordings when we amend the legislation.

key_points.point: The ministry is reviewing appropriate penalties for animal welfare and cruelty offences, including those applying to animal-related businesses.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: We are also reviewing the appropriate penalties for animal welfare and cruelty offences, including those that apply to animal-related businesses.

key_points.point: The Code of Animal Welfare includes not leaving animals unattended in rooms, unsupervised.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: that includes not leaving animals unattended in rooms, unsupervised, as the Member had mentioned

key_points.point: Breaches of the Code can support prosecution under the ABA, including section 42 for unnecessary pain or suffering and section 41 for failure of duty of care.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: where unnecessary pain or suffering has been found to be inflicted on the animal, that is section 42 of the ABA, or failure of duty of care is found, section 41 of the ABA

key_points.point: The public can contact AVS at 1800 4761 600.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
